mainTopic: Cancelling and releasing vows on שבת and at night
overview: The גמרא quotes a משנה in מסכת שבת. It says a husband or father may cancel vows (הפרה) on שבת, and one may ask a חכם to release vows that are needed for שבת. First it asks whether הפרה on שבת is allowed only for שבת needs. The answer depends on a dispute between תנאים about how long the window for cancelling lasts. If the window is 'all day', any vow may be cancelled on שבת. If it is 'twenty-four hours' (מעת לעת), only vows needed for שבת are cancelled on שבת. Next, a story shows that vows needed for שבת may be released on שבת even if there was time to ask before שבת. אביי rejects רב יוסף's idea that three laymen may not release vows on שבת, because releasing vows does not look like a court case. Then a ruling of רב is reworded to teach that a חכם may release vows at night. רבי אבא questions whether רב really held this, so the גמרא begins a story about רב releasing a vow for רבה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: vows may be cancelled on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת שבת: a husband or father may cancel vows on שבת, and one may ask a חכם to release vows that are for the needs of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: vows may be cancelled on שבת, and one may ask a חכם about vows that are needed for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another מסכת as the starting point for a new question. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions two different things. הפרה is when a husband or father cancels a vow. שאלה is when a חכם releases a vow. Only the second one is clearly limited to 'the needs of שבת', so it is unclear whether that limit also applies to הפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, in a משנה from a different place
Cancel (a husband or father cancelling a vow)
Ask a חכם to release a vow (התרה)
For the needs of שבת

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת שבת (157a).

phrases.english: One may cancel vows on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: This means a husband or father cancelling his wife's or daughter's vow.

phrases.english: and one may ask a sage to release vows
that are for the needs of Shabbat.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: הפרת נדרים is allowed on שבת, and שאלה for vows is allowed when they are for the needs of שבת.

steps.title: Does the 'שבת needs' limit apply to cancelling too?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether הפרה on שבת is allowed only for vows that affect שבת, or for any vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: may vows be cancelled on שבת only for the needs of שבת, or maybe even when they are not needed for שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question about how far the משנה's permission goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for the needs of שבת' might cover both parts of the משנה, or only the second part about asking a חכם. The question is whether a husband may cancel a vow on שבת that only matters for later in the week.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Or maybe

phrases.english: They asked:
Do we cancel vows on Shabbat
only for the needs of Shabbat,
or maybe even when it is not needed for Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the permission in the משנה goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether הפרה on שבת is limited to vows that concern שבת.

steps.title: רב זוטי's ברייתא: only for שבת needs
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטי from the school of רב פפי teaches a ברייתא that vows may be cancelled on שבת only for the needs of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רב זוטי of the school of רב פפי taught: vows are cancelled on שבת only for the needs of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to answer the question directly: only vows needed for שבת may be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא applies the 'שבת needs' limit to הפרה as well. If it stands, a husband must wait until after שבת to cancel a vow that does not affect שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a source as an answer
That he taught (a ברייתא)
Of the school of רב פפי

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי רַב זוּטֵי דְּבֵי רַב פַּפֵּי:
phrases.english: for Rav Zuti of the school of Rav Pappi taught:
Vows are not cancelled
except for the needs of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On שבת, vows may be cancelled only for the needs of שבת.

steps.title: רב אשי: our משנה says 'until nightfall' with no limits
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges the ברייתא from our משנה, which says a vow made close to nightfall can be cancelled until dark. If non-שבת vows could not be cancelled on שבת, mentioning nightfall would make no sense, because on שבת he could not cancel them even during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: we did not learn it that way. The משנה says: if she vowed close to nightfall, he may cancel it until it gets dark. If only שבת-needs vows may be cancelled and others may not, why mention nightfall? Even during the day he cannot cancel what is not for שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי raises a difficulty from our own משנה against the ברייתא of רב זוטי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה gives one simple rule: the husband may cancel until nightfall. It makes no exception for שבת. If רב זוטי were right, then on שבת the time limit would not matter at all for non-שבת vows, since they could not be cancelled at any point that day. So the משנה seems to assume that any vow may be cancelled, even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We did not learn it that way
Close to nightfall
Why specifically this case?
Yes / no

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said,
We did not learn it that way:
If she vowed close to nightfall —
he may cancel it for her until it gets dark.
And if you say that for the needs of Shabbat — yes,
not for the needs of Shabbat — no,
why mention nightfall specifically?
Even during the day
he cannot cancel something that is not needed!
phrases.notes: In other words, on שבת the nightfall deadline would mean nothing for these vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, הָא לָא תְּנַן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of רב זוטי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that only שבת-needs vows may be cancelled on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה gives nightfall as the only deadline, with no exception for שבת. That implies every vow may be cancelled during the day, even on שבת.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים about the deadline
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this depends on a dispute between תנאים. The first view says cancelling is allowed for the whole day the husband hears the vow. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון say it is allowed for twenty-four hours (מעת לעת).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. One view: cancelling vows is allowed all day. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said: for twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי by saying our משנה and the ברייתא follow different תנאים. The next step explains how this dispute connects to שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה ('until nightfall') follows the view that cancelling is allowed only for that calendar day. The other view gives a full twenty-four hours from when he heard the vow. This difference in the deadline is what decides the שבת question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
The whole day, ending at nightfall
From one time to the same time the next day, twenty-four hours

steps.confusionAlert: 'כל היום' ends at nightfall, so it can be very short if he heard the vow late in the day. 'מעת לעת' is always a full twenty-four hours, no matter when he heard the vow.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between Tannaim:
Cancelling vows is allowed all day,
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said:
For twenty-four hours.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: the משנה and the ברייתא follow different views.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: That everyone agrees on one rule for cancelling vows on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שבת question depends on how long the window for cancelling lasts.

steps.title: How each view decides the שבת question
steps.stepSummary: According to 'all day', he must be allowed to cancel any vow on שבת, even one not needed for שבת. Otherwise his window would close and the chance would be lost. According to 'twenty-four hours', only שבת-needs vows are cancelled on שבת, and the others can wait until after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'all day', yes, but no longer: he may cancel even what is not for שבת. According to the one who says 'twenty-four hours': for שבת needs, yes; not for שבת needs, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by showing how each view in the dispute leads to a different rule for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under 'all day', if he waited until after שבת, the deadline would already have passed, so he is allowed to cancel any vow on שבת. That matches our משנה. Under 'מעת לעת', he usually still has time after שבת, so only urgent שבת-related vows are cancelled on שבת itself. That matches רב זוטי's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
More, longer
He cancels

steps.whatToRemember: The שבת rule depends on the deadline. If the window closes at nightfall ('כל היום'), any vow may be cancelled on שבת. If it lasts twenty-four hours ('מעת לעת'), only שבת-needs vows are cancelled on שבת. Our משנה follows the first view, and רב זוטי's ברייתא follows the second.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a rule about שבת can really depend on a separate question, here how long the window for cancelling a vow lasts.

phrases.english: According to the one who says 'all day'
yes, but no longer —
phrases.notes: He means: the window is only that day, so if he waits until after שבת he loses his chance.

phrases.english: he may cancel even what is not for the needs of Shabbat.
According to the one who says 'twenty-four hours',
for the needs of Shabbat — yes,
not for the needs of Shabbat — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the dispute in step 5 leads to two different rules for שבת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה follows 'כל היום' and allows cancelling any vow on שבת. רב זוטי's ברייתא follows 'מעת לעת' and allows it only for שבת needs.

steps.title: A quoted rule: asking for release of vows on שבת for שבת-needs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the second half of the משנה from step 1, which allows asking a חכם to release vows on שבת when the vows are needed for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may ask a sage to release vows that are needed for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from a משנה in מסכת שבת. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about הפרה, where a husband or father cancels a vow. This line is about a different process, שאלה, where the person who vowed asks a חכם to release the vow. The משנה allows this on שבת only when the vow affects שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: They ask a sage to release a vow (התרת חכם)
For the needs of שבת
Vows

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up נִשְׁאָלִין with מְפִירִין. הפרה is done by a husband or father; שאלה is when the person who made the vow asks a חכם to undo it. This part of the sugya is about שאלה.

phrases.english: And one may ask a sage about vows
phrases.notes: This is a line from a משנה in מסכת שבת. 'Ask' here means asking a sage to release the vow.

phrases.english: that are for the needs of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from a husband's הפרה on שבת to asking a חכם for release on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם may release vows on שבת if they are needed for שבת.

steps.title: Only if there was no time before שבת, or even if there was?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether this permission is only for someone who had no chance to ask before שבת, or even for someone who did have the chance.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is this only when they did not have time before שבת, or perhaps even when they did have time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how far the permission from the משנה goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think the leniency is only for emergencies, when there was no time before שבת. Or it could be a general permission, even for someone who could have asked earlier but did not. The גמרא wants to know which.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
Free time, a chance to do something
Or perhaps

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Is it when they did not have time,
phrases.notes: He means: no time to ask a sage before שבת started.

phrases.english: or perhaps even when they did have time?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the scope of the rule quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether release of שבת-needed vows on שבת is limited to people who had no chance to ask before שבת.

steps.title: The story of רב זוטרא's son shows: even if there was time
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים released the vows of the son of רב זוטרא בריה דרב זעירא on שבת, even vows he could have asked about before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the חכמים took care of the vows of the son of רב זוטרא son of רב זעירא on שבת, even vows they had time to deal with while it was still day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a real story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים released vows on שבת even though there had been time before שבת. So the permission is not only for emergencies. Any vow needed for שבת may be released on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source that answers the question)
They attended to, took care of
While it was still day (before שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: Vows needed for שבת may be released on שבת even if the person could have asked before שבת.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that the Rabbis attended
phrases.notes: They released his vows on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: לִבְרֵיהּ דְּרַב זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב זְעֵירָא
phrases.english: to the son of Rav Zutra, son of Rav Zeira,
even for vows that they had time for
while it was still day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even if there was time before שבת, vows needed for שבת may be released on שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף: only a single expert, not three laymen, on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף thought that on שבת a vow may be released by one expert, but not by three ordinary people, since that looks like a court case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף thought to say: vows may be released on שבת by a single expert, yes; by three laymen, no, because it looks like a court judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף suggests a limit on who may release vows on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow can be released by one expert or by three non-experts. Courts may not judge on שבת. רב יוסף worries that a group of three looks like a court, so he would forbid it on שבת. The word 'סבר' hints that this view will not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (a view that will be rejected)
A single expert sage
Three ordinary people (not experts)
It looks like a court judgment

phrases.english: Rav Yosef thought to say:
Vows may be asked about on Shabbat,
with a single expert, yes;
with three laymen, no,
because it looks like a court judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new limit on the permission to release vows on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, only a single expert may release vows; three laymen may not, since it looks like a court.

steps.title: אביי: releasing vows does not look like a court at all
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף, since vows may be released standing, by relatives, and at night, things a court can never do.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Since we hold that vows may be released even standing, even by relatives, and even at night, it does not look like a court judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב יוסף's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real court sits, may not include relatives, and judges by day. Releasing vows is allowed in all those ways, so nobody would confuse it with a court. Therefore even three laymen may release vows on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Since we hold
Standing (a court normally sits)
Relatives (who may not be judges)

steps.whatToRemember: Release of vows on שבת is allowed even by three laymen, because vow-release does not look like a court.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Since we hold that it may be done even standing,
even by relatives, and even at night,
phrases.notes: A real court must sit, may not use relatives, and judges by day. Vow-release breaks all three.

phrases.english: it does not look like a court judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: כֵּיוָן דִּסְבִירָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's reasoning from step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole limit of 'only a single expert on שבת'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף assumed three laymen look like a court, but vow-release has none of a court's formal features.

steps.title: רב: the הלכה is that vows may be cancelled at night
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes רב הונא in the name of רב that one may cancel (הפרה) vows at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא in the name of רב: The הלכה is that one may cancel vows at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from רב about doing vow-cancelling at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As written, the ruling says a husband or father can do הפרה at night. The next step will ask why this needed to be said at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling
They cancel (הפרה, done by husband or father)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
The halacha is: one may cancel vows at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of nighttime, which אביי just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הפרה of vows may be done at night.

steps.title: But our משנה already says this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say it, since our משנה already teaches that a vow made on Friday night can be cancelled that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is our משנה: 'She vowed on Friday night'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה speaks of a woman who vowed on Friday night and is cancelled that night. So we already know הפרה works at night. Why would רב need to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: But this is already our משנה!
Friday night

phrases.english: But this is already our mishna:
"She vowed on Shabbat evening"!
phrases.notes: In our משנה, the husband or father can cancel such a vow that same night.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that הפרה may be done at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה already shows הפרה at night, so the ruling adds nothing.

steps.title: Correct the ruling: a חכם may release vows at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes רב's ruling to be about שאלה: one may ask a חכם to release a vow at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: The הלכה is that one may ask a חכם to release vows at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רב's ruling so it teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is not about הפרה, which the משנה already covers. It is about a חכם releasing a vow, which we might have thought needs daytime like a court. רב teaches that it may be done at night, matching אביי's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (change the wording)
At night

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is that a חכם may release vows at night. This is different from a husband's הפרה, which our משנה already covers.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
The halacha is: one may ask a sage about vows at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by changing the wording of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling was about a husband's הפרה at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ruling is about asking a חכם for release at night, which the משנה does not teach.

steps.title: רבי אבא checks whether רב really said it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks רב הונא directly whether רב actually ruled that vows may be released at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רב הונא: Did רב really say this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא is double-checking the source of the ruling. He wants to know whether רב himself actually said that a vow may be released at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ruling was reported as 'רב הונא in the name of רב'. Now רבי אבא asks whether רב truly said it. This opens a short exchange about how sure we can be of רב's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: So, like this (this ruling)
He said to him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rav Huna:
Did Rav say this?
phrases.notes: 'This' is the ruling from the last step: a vow may be released by a חכם at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the attribution of the ruling that Step 14 set up.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב himself actually stated the ruling about releasing vows at night.

steps.title: רב הונא: רב stayed silent
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that רב did not say it outright. He was silent when the ruling was said in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: רב was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains how he knows רב's view. רב did not say the ruling himself; he just kept quiet when it was said in front of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Staying quiet when a ruling is said in front of you usually means you agree with it. So רב הונא is telling us that רב's opinion was learned from his silence, not from his own words.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent, he kept quiet

phrases.english: He said to him: He was silent.
phrases.notes: רב heard the ruling and did not object.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's question in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב did not state it outright; he stayed silent when it was said, which suggests agreement.

steps.title: Did you say 'silent' or 'drinking'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks whether רב הונא said 'אישתיק' (he was silent) or 'שתי' (he was drinking), two words that sound alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: Did you say 'he was silent', or did you say 'he was drinking'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא is not sure he heard correctly. The two Aramaic words sound almost the same, and the meaning changes a lot depending on which one was said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב was silent, his silence shows he agreed. But if רב was drinking, he was busy, so his quiet proves nothing about his opinion. The whole question is whether we can really count this ruling as רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He was drinking
You are saying

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אבא is just fussing over a word. 'Silent' means רב agreed; 'drinking' means רב may not have paid attention, so we would not know his view at all.

phrases.english: He said to him: Are you saying 'he was silent,'
or are you saying 'he was drinking'?
phrases.notes: If רב was drinking, he was busy, so his quiet does not show he agreed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אישתיק קא אמרת או שתי קאמרת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the exact word רב הונא used in Step 16, which decides whether רב's silence counts as agreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב was silent (agreeing) or drinking (busy, so no proof of agreement).

steps.title: A story about רב releasing רבה's vow
steps.stepSummary: To find out what רב really held, the גמרא starts a story from רב איקא בר אבין: רב took care of releasing a vow for רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא בר אבין said: רב took care of releasing a vow for רבה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It begins a story about something רב actually did, to show his real opinion. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב's silence was unclear, the גמרא turns to what רב did in practice. If the story shows רב releasing a vow at night, that would prove he held the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Attended to, took care of (here: releasing a vow)
The אמורא who tells the story

phrases.english: Rav Ika bar Avin said:
Rav attended to Rabba
phrases.notes: רב worked on releasing a vow רבה had made.
